unmapped_findings: For the sample condition 1050 °C/0.1 s^-1 the calculated Zener-Hollomon parameter is lnZ = 58.60 (Table 1).
The material is a Fe-Mn-Al-C steel of a single forging-billet heat with composition (mass fraction, %) 1.46 C, 25.14 Mn, 10 Al, 0.053 Nb, balance Fe (b0018).

The paper's recommended window for obtaining a fine and uniform grain structure is 950-1000 °C/0.01-0.1 s^-1 and 1050-1100 °C/1-10 s^-1; the present condition (1050 °C/0.1 s^-1) lies outside both windows, so it is not identified as giving a fine uniform DRX structure (b0012, b0065, b0086).

DRX behavior: the steel is negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive; peak stress decreases with decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature; at 0.01 s^-1 peak stress falls from 305.4 MPa (900 °C) to 53.8 MPa (1150 °C) (82% reduction) and at 10 s^-1 it falls 73% over the same range (b0024).
The DRX activation energy of the steel is 669.844 kJ mol^-1 (b0032).
DRX average grain size increases with decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature; at 1150 °C and 0.01 s^-1 the grain size exceeds 70 µm (coarse-grain structure) (b0063, figure_010).
The material was confirmed to show reproducibility of the reported experimental phenomena under identical experimental conditions for the same steel batch/composition (b0018, b0012).
